title: [RFE] Allow importing a RKE2 cluster without immediately upgrading it
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
We're in the situation where we manage clusters in Rancher that we don't have operational responsibility for, which means we should never start a version upgrade. Rancher's behavior of auto-upgrading any imported RKE2 cluster causes problems for us.

Imho importing an existing cluster into rancher should do just that - import it. It should not automatically start upgrading the cluster without providing users a way of cancelling the upgrade.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Let upgrades be optional instead of mandatory

**Describe alternatives you've considered**


**Additional context**

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
@reporter , thank you for reporting this issue.

Could you please provide steps to reproduce this behavior as simply importing RKE2 cluster should NOT be upgrading K8s version on it. Full disclosure - there was a report of an issue where the functionality we have that allows upgrading imported RKE2/K3s clusters kicked off the "upgrade" the cluster to the same version it's already running - but what you're stating sounds like Rancher upgrading imported RKE2 cluster to a version that is newer than the version it's running already. For the issue I've mentioned we were not successful in reproducing it and added extra logging to the controller responsible for kicking off such upgrades as part of https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/46147 that made it into v2.9.1+ / v2.10.0+ - so hopefully you can reproduce it on these versions and provide DEBUG level logs.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Hi, thanks for responding. My rancher cluster is on 2.9.2 and we still have a a couple of those "external" clusters to import. Where would I retrieve the debug logs? from the rancher server pods or from the cluster being imported?

The upgrade for the first imported cluster failed btw, because these clusters are partially airgapped so they're unable to reach out and pull in any images they want etc. I killed all upgrade jobs etc, but the cluster still reports it being upgraded:

![Screenshot from 2024-11-18 16-23-42](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7a9e633f-43e2-4cdb-a2f8-bc9af02295d6)

I can see this in the cluster conditions:
```
 - lastUpdateTime: '2024-11-13T09:49:57Z'
      message: worker node [xxxx] being upgraded
      status: Unknown
      type: Upgraded
```
am I okay to delete this, in order clean up the uggrade status?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
@reporter , the logs we're interested in here are from Rancher pods. Please note that you will want to enable debug logging, see https://<redacted-host>/troubleshooting/other-troubleshooting-tips/logging for more info.

It would be great if you could then import a new cluster after that and provide those logs to help us better understand why Rancher is trying to upgrade K8s version on it. Please also provide a (potentially sanitized) YAML of corresponding `<redacted-host>` object.

Regarding the "clean up" question it may be getting rather tricky depending on what kind of clean up you've already done. Could you please clarify what was already done?
At a glance it may be acceptable to set that condition's status to `True` and clear the message (essentially doing what https://github.com/rancher/rancher/blob/v2.9.2/pkg/controllers/management/k3sbasedupgrade/k3sbased_upgrade_handler.go#L67-L72 is doing on successful upgrade) but I'm worried about upgrade plans that may still be present on the **downstream (imported)** clusters (`<redacted-host>` objects) - you may need to delete them as well.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Thanks, I will try and prep for that and import another cluster during next week.

As for the failed upgrade of the already imported cluster: from what we could see, Rancher fires off a kubernetes Job that performs the upgrade. For us this job just hung there, as it was unable to pull down the required image due to the fact that the cluster does not have unlimited internet access. From what I can remember, I deleted the job - I believe I had do that a couple of times probably due to some retries that kept recreating it. It was a bit stressful at the time since we didn't know if we'd botched the entire cluster so I did not keep a clear track. Will do that for the next cluster we import, and enable debug logging as you requested.

these are clusters that are provisioned by a service provider, so we don't have all that much insight into how they're provisioned and why data is reported as it is I'm afraid. We (as customers) are allowed to use Rancher as a management proxy, but we're note allowed to perform node upgrades or other cluster-imacting management (although we technically have permissions to do so, we're contractually obligated not to).

I'll provide the output of the cluster objects you asked for in a separate comment. 

Thanks again for following up on this with us, it's very much appreciated!

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
@reporter , ah, that explains it then and then you're running into https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/45030. Could you please follow steps from https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/45030#issuecomment-2341340501 to see if if allows you to work around the issue?

Meanwhile, we're planning to:
* Address immediate bug https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/45030 - TBD the exact approach, but at this point we're leaning towards skipping any Windows nodes when determining whether cluster K8s version upgrade is needed and skipping Windows nodes if upgrade was in fact kicked off (imported RKE2 clusters with Windows nodes are not officially supported but it makes sense to improve UX even if this happens).
* As part of https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/41010 we will allow disabling K8s version management for imported clusters (regardless of whether they contain Windows nodes or not).

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
An update on this:
- today we updated to rancher 2.10.2. At the same time we set `CATTLE_FEATURES:managed-system-upgrade-controller=false` in the rancher server helm chart's extra env vars, and verified that these get set on the rancher pods on the mgmt cluster
- we then removed one of the "problematic clusters" from rancher.
- we then re-added it (same name but new id, so rancher should treat it as a completely "unknown" cluster).
- yet again, the cluster went straight into "Upgrading"

I guess it was our understanding that rancher should no longer auto-update clusters with this new version and feature flag set but I guess I misunderstood something..

We could se a few "helm-operation" pods starting and completing, but these seem to be related to rancher webhook and other things. Otherwise there's nothing in the cluster waiting for anything as far as I can see, and no "plan" objects. But still, the cluster is stuck "Upgrading".....

The only reference I can find are various status objects in the various cluster objects, like:
```
  - lastUpdateTime: "2025-02-02T20:19:23Z"
    message: cluster is being upgraded
    status: Unknown
    type: Upgraded

```
If I delete these, they just pop back. 
So there's still _something_ that marks the cluster as "Upgrading", tho we no longer see any trace of any form of update actually kicked off. So that's good, but we're still looking for a way to get rid of the "Upgrading" message on the cluster.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
@reporter , apologies for not responding to your earlier messages - unfortunately there is limited time available to assist with troubleshooting community issues.

On `CATTLE_FEATURES:managed-system-upgrade-controller=false` - this setting doesn't turn off SUC-based upgrade feature but instead allow disabling migration of SUC installation from deprecated `system-charts` mechanism to new mechanism implemented in https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/42448 (see https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/42448#issuecomment-2477309567 and the conversation that follows).

Now, your immediate issue should be addressed with the fix to https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/48960 that we're _targeting_ for v2.10.3 (there is a high chance it will make it in, but can't make any guarantees of course).

And then https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/41010 _targeting_ v2.11.0 should allow to completely disable version management for imported RKE2/K3s clusters which should properly support your use case:
> we're not allowed to perform node upgrades or other cluster-impacting management (although we technically have permissions to do so, we're contractually obligated not to)

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: I understand, I must have misunderstood the other tickets when I read them. Thanks for taking the time to respond, it's appreciated!

comments.body: @reporter , thank you for understanding. Closing this issue as it's covered by a combination of https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/45030 and https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/41010.
